question_text: According to this unit, is it correct to equate the system unit with the CPU?
option_b: No -- the CPU is only one component within the system unit
option_c: The system unit is smaller than the CPU
option_d: The CPU contains the system unit
explanation: The unit clarifies this is a common novice confusion: the CPU is a component within the system unit, not the whole system unit itself.

question_text: Which chip contains data written during manufacturing that tells the CPU what to do when the PC is switched on, and retains this data even when powered off?
explanation: Read-only memory (ROM) chips have manufacturer-written data that tells the CPU what to do at startup, and this data remains even when the PC is off.

question_text: Which type of memory is lost entirely when the PC is switched off, and is used to hold running programs and their data?
explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) holds the program and its data while running, but anything held in RAM is lost when the PC is switched off.

question_text: Which component, made of expensive and very fast memory chips, stores data/instructions the CPU will look at next, speeding up work significantly?
explanation: Cache Memory consists of expensive and very fast memory chips that store data or instructions the CPU will look at next, speeding up work considerably.

question_text: The computer's most important single component, doing all the 'thinking' and running programs, is called the:
explanation: The Microprocessor, or Central Processing Unit (CPU), is the computer's most important single item, doing all the thinking and running programs.

question_text: CPU speed is measured in which unit?
explanation: The speed of a CPU is measured in megahertz (MHz), where one megahertz equals one million clock ticks per second.

question_text: According to the CPU generation table in this unit, which CPU generation is associated with the Pentium (1993-95)?
explanation: The 5th Generation CPU table lists the Pentium (1993-95) with roughly 3,100,000 transistors.

question_text: According to this unit, all electronic components in a PC are mounted on a piece of fiberglass called the:
explanation: All electronic components in a PC are mounted on a piece of fiberglass called the motherboard, which insulates each component while connecting them electrically.

question_text: The two sizes of floppy disks discussed in this unit are:
explanation: Floppy disks come in two sizes: either 5 1/4 or 3 1/2 inches in diameter.

question_text: Low-capacity floppy disks are generally labeled with which designation?
explanation: Low-capacity disks are generally labeled DS/DD, standing for 'double sided/double density'.

question_text: The intelligent computer keyboard has four major divisions. Which of the following is one of them?
explanation: The intelligent computer keyboard has four major divisions: Function keys, Alphanumeric keys, Numeric keys, and Control keys.

question_text: In most software packages, which function key is traditionally used to run the HELP program?
explanation: In most software packages, the function key F1 is used to run the HELP program.

question_text: Which key, when pressed, activates the capital letters on alphanumeric keys and the upper part of each key?
explanation: When the Shift key is pressed, capital letters on the alphanumeric keys are activated, along with the upper-part characters.

question_text: Which key combination is used to restart or reboot the computer, according to this unit?
explanation: To restart or reboot the computer, one presses the Alt, Ctrl and Del keys simultaneously.

question_text: Pressing the Insert key toggles the keyboard between which two modes?
explanation: Pressing the Insert key puts the keyboard in insert mode; pressing it again returns to overstrike (typeover) mode.

question_text: There are three basic types of printers discussed in this unit. Which of the following is one of them?
explanation: The three basic types of printers discussed are laser printers, inkjet printers, and dot-matrix printers.

question_text: Which type of printer combines a magnetic roller with powdered ink called toner to produce high-quality images?
explanation: Laser printers combine a magnetic roller with powdered ink called toner to transfer high-quality characters or images onto a page.

question_text: Which type of printer is described as the cheapest, hammering small pins against an inked ribbon to create characters out of dots?
explanation: Dot-matrix printers, the cheapest printers available, create text and images by hammering several small pins against an inked ribbon.

question_text: VGA and SVGA are acronyms describing what property of a monitor?
explanation: VGA and SVGA generally refer to how many dots (pixels) in each direction the monitor can display -- this is called the monitor's resolution.

question_text: A scanner works by dividing an image into microscopic rows and columns and measuring how much light reflects from each intersection, recording each reflection as a:
explanation: Each reflection recorded by a scanner is called a dot, or picture element (pixel).

question_text: Which type of scanner looks and behaves like a photocopier, allowing you to lay an item on a glass plate while the scanning head passes below?
explanation: Flatbed scanners look and behave like a photocopier, with items placed on a glass plate and the scanning head passing below.

question_text: According to this unit, why are air conditioners needed in a computing environment?
option_a: To make the room look professional
option_b: To condition the temperature and prevent dust (which can bridge electronic circuits)
option_d: To increase the computer's processing speed
explanation: Air conditioners are needed to condition the temperature and prevent dust, since dust is metallic and can bridge electronic circuits, causing damage.

question_text: What is the primary purpose of a voltage stabilizer in a computing environment, according to this unit?
option_b: To protect against damage from sudden power cuts and surges
explanation: A voltage stabilizer helps protect computing equipment from damage due to power surges, since a sudden power cut can halt the computer and cause file damage.

question_text: According to this unit, what voltage do computers in the United States typically operate on, requiring a transformer to step down Nigeria's 240V supply?
explanation: Computers in the USA are built to operate on 110V; a voltage transformer is needed to step down Nigeria's 240V supply to 110V for such computers.

question_text: Which auxiliary device converts raw public electricity into a fine line, stores electrical energy, and releases it to the computer during a power outage?
explanation: An Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) conditions the incoming voltage, stores electrical energy when power is available, and releases it during outages.

question_text: According to this unit's conclusion, how should the UPS itself be protected?
option_b: By a voltage stabilizer, which is rugged and less expensive
option_c: By keeping it unplugged at all times
explanation: The UPS is itself an expensive resource and should be protected by a voltage stabilizer, which is rugged and less expensive.

question_text: Computer software can be divided into two major groups. Which of the following pairs correctly identifies them?
explanation: Computer software could be divided into two major groups: System Software (Programs) and Application Software (Programs).

question_text: An operating system's primary goal, according to this unit, is:
option_c: To eliminate the need for application programs
option_d: To slow down processing for stability
explanation: The primary goal of an operating system is convenience for the user -- making computing easier than it would be without one.

question_text: Which type of operating system collects jobs into a batch and processes them with no user interaction during processing, measuring 'turnaround time'?
explanation: In a batch processing operating system, jobs are collected into a batch with no user interaction during processing; turnaround time is measured.

question_text: Which type of operating system is designed for applications like airline reservations or nuclear power station monitoring, where response time is critical to prevent disaster?
explanation: Real time operating systems service applications where response time is of the essence to prevent error or disaster, such as airline reservations.

question_text: A system that allows more than one active user program to be stored in main memory simultaneously is called:
explanation: A multiprogramming operating system allows more than one active user program (or part of a program) to be stored in main memory simultaneously.

question_text: Which operating system component is responsible for the creation and deletion of both user and system processes?
explanation: Process management is responsible for the creation and deletion of both user and system processes, along with suspension, resumption, and synchronization.

question_text: Which operating system component provides a uniform logical view of information storage, abstracting from physical device properties?
explanation: File management provides a uniform logical view of information storage, defining the logical storage unit called a file, mapped onto physical devices.

question_text: Which operating system component is the primary interface between the user and the rest of the system, sometimes called the 'shell' in UNIX?
explanation: The command interpreter is the primary interface between the user and the rest of the system, called the shell in UNIX.

question_text: The suite of languages that translate other computer languages into machine language are called:
explanation: The suites of languages that translate other languages to machine language are called Language Translators.

question_text: Which type of language translator accepts a program in a source language and reads, translates, and executes it line by line?
explanation: An Interpreter accepts a program in a source language, reads, translates and executes it line by line into machine language.

question_text: Which of the following is listed as one of the stages of compilation?
explanation: The stages in compilation include lexical analysis, syntax analysis, semantic analysis, and code generation.

question_text: Utility software performs which of the following operations?
option_a: File conversion, file copy, and housekeeping operations
explanation: Utility software performs operations such as file conversion, file copy, and housekeeping operations like clearing storage areas.

question_text: Application software can be subdivided into which two classes?
explanation: Application software could be subdivided into two classes: Generalized (e.g. word processors, spreadsheets) and User-defined software.

question_text: Which application software category is used for producing letters, mailing lists, and reports, with examples like WordPerfect and MS-Word?
explanation: A Word Processor is used to create, edit, save and print reports, letters, mailing lists, and more, with examples including WordPerfect and MS-Word.

question_text: Which application software category is designed mainly for numerical figures and reports, using formulas, sum, and average functions?
explanation: Spreadsheet software is designed mainly for numerical figures and reports, with formulas, sum, average functions, and automatic recalculation.

question_text: Which application software category is used for designing, setting up, and managing an organized collection of data?
explanation: Database Packages are software for designing, setting up and managing a database -- an organized collection of data.
